purpose: Targeted size/distance/viewpoint boundary checks after appearance improvements
selection: Original utterances selected from explicit boundary semantics and zero-API full-scene geometry before model calls. Development checks, not holdout accuracy. Tie rows selected for ambiguity; evaluation IDs do not constrain inference.
runtime_input: Original query plus full prepared scene with annotated categories/boxes; no target or stimulus IDs in worker input

rows.acceptance_focus: Explicit all-category largest comparison; verify comparison pool and actual size execution before acceptance

rows.query: the shorter of the two dresser
rows.acceptance_focus: Named of-the-two comparison stays unknown until the instance set is bound; no global category substitution

rows.query: The trash can closest to the chair.
rows.acceptance_focus: 0.005883m center-distance tie to one chair plus multiple-reference interpretations must preserve ambiguity and not force a winner

rows.query: The box closest to the door.
rows.acceptance_focus: Two doors imply different nearest boxes; each anchor ranking independent and no mean-anchor origin

rows.query: Facing the foot of the bed, the dresser in the lower right corner.
rows.acceptance_focus: Facing the foot of the bed requires intrinsic orientation; preserve exact phrase and explicit unsupported/unknown boundary

rows.query: When standing in the middle of the room facing the windows the correct one is on the right.
rows.acceptance_focus: Explicit middle-room origin and facing window group; all legal language frames must jointly support target
